> Alex — thanks for taking a look. Our legal team pushed a handful of redlines in the Order Form/Exhibit A that we think are necessary for StellarSys to move forward with productization.

Thanks, Sandra — appreciate the clarity and the quick turnaround. High level from our side: Redwood's standard is to provide customers a broad commercial license to use outputs for productization; we don't usually do an automatic assignment of title for generated outputs. That said, we do offer tailored commercial paths for customers that need stronger rights (assignment or exclusive productization rights) typically in exchange for additional consideration and an evidence/controls gated process.

To move this forward I attached a short proposal (redline-proposal-alex-20260512.docx) with two options:
- Option A (default): Non-exclusive perpetual license to use outputs for productization; customer retains rights to their input and to derivative works they create.
- Option B (premium): Conditional assignment/expanded rights for specific product lines after delivery of agreed telemetry/evidence package + security attestation; requires procurement approval and a fee schedule addendum.

For telemetry evidence we are usually satisfied with:
- a sample set of anonymized request/response pairs (redacted PII),
- aggregated token counts by day and feature, and
- a short runbook describing how data was captured (timestamp ranges and sampling method).

Key asks for StellarSys from Redwood's side if you pursue Option B: 
1) Define the exact product lines/features you want covered by expanded rights.
2) Provide the evidence bundle into our secure evidence S3 bucket or via a SharePoint link (we'll give upload instructions).
3) Agree on a limited retention window and data minimization language for the evidence; Redwood will not use the evidence as training material.

If that framework works I'll loop in our legal lead (Laura) and revenue ops (Rishi) to draft concrete redline language and the procurement checklist. Can you confirm target product lines and whether procurement is ok with an evidence upload into a secure bucket?

Thanks — Alex
Alex Martinez

Alex — thanks for the clear summary. Draft thoughts below and attached are two short snippets you can drop into the Order Form/Exhibit A.

Short answer on assignment vs license: Redwood's baseline remains a license. For customers that need stronger commercialization rights, we can offer a conditional grant of expanded rights (including a narrow assignment) that vests only after the evidence and attestation workflow completes and the parties execute a short addendum. We'll want to avoid a blanket assignment across all outputs — instead we should limit to named product lines or use-cases (language suggested below).

Suggested contract language (high level):
- "Productization Rights Addendum": Customer may request expanded rights for specified Product Features by submitting an evidence package to Redwood's secure evidence portal. Upon Redwood's verification of the package and execution of the Productization Addendum, Customer will receive the expanded license/assignment scope limited to the specified Product Features and for the term set forth in the Addendum.
- Evidence scope: Anonymized request/response samples; aggregated token telemetry; a short capture runbook; and a security attestation (SOC2 or equivalent). Evidence will be retained for verification for no longer than 90 days and will not be added to Redwood model training data.

Operational checklist for procurement (for Rishi):
1) Customer identifies Product Features and submits evidence bundle to evidence portal.
2) Security/Engineering performs verification within 5 business days and certifies via signed attestation.
3) Legal reviews and triggers Productization Addendum; commercial lead raises the one-time fee invoice if Option B applies.

Edge notes: 
- If StellarSys insists on immediate assignment we should push back and require (a) higher fee and (b) a capped geographic/market limitation and (c) IP indemnity carveouts.
- Recommend we keep telemetry format flexible but insist on redaction of PII and cryptographically verifiable upload (S3 pre-signed + audit log).

I've attached a short text snippet (excerpt-legal-suggestion.txt) with the proposed wording. Happy to refine — will set aside time at 3pm if you want to review by voice.

Laura Bennett
